entry.title: a small guide to web performance
entry.content:
Every few months web performance bites me again. This is what finally stuck.

why it matters

Web performance shows up across web work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Optimise for the reader who shows up six months from now with no context.
  • Start with the smallest thing that works, then make it boring on purpose.
  • Write it down once, link to it everywhere.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

entry.content:
I spent a while getting web performance wrong. Here is the version that works for me.

why it matters

Web performance shows up across web work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Start with the smallest thing that works, then make it boring on purpose.
  • Most of the value is in deleting, not adding.
  • Measure before you change anything; intuition is a poor profiler.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

entry.content:
Every few months web performance bites me again. This is what finally stuck.

why it matters

Web performance shows up across web work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Start with the smallest thing that works, then make it boring on purpose.
  • Make the default path the correct path so nobody has to remember the rule.
  • The fix that survives is the one the next person can understand.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

entry.title: web performance in practice
entry.content:
Short post: web performance is one of those things that looks simple until it isn’t.

why it matters

Web performance shows up across web work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Measure before you change anything; intuition is a poor profiler.
  • Most of the value is in deleting, not adding.
  • If it is hard to test, that is the design telling you something.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.
